issue_body:
Users can only browse notes by date, so finding an old note means scrolling.

Add `GET /notes/search?q=<terms>` returning the caller's notes whose title or body contains every term, newest first, at most 50 per page with a `next_cursor`. Another user's notes never appear. An empty `q` returns `400` with error code `empty_query`. The web client calls it on every keystroke, so search must respond fast enough for search-as-you-type.

plan.summary: Add full-text note search backed by a GIN index, paginated by cursor.

approach.description: Add migration 0047 creating a GIN index on to_tsvector('simple', title || ' ' || body), with a down migration dropping it.
Add SearchNotes in internal/store/notes_search.go: plainto_tsquery so every term must match, filter owner_id to the caller, ORDER BY created_at DESC, and fetch 51 rows to derive next_cursor.
Add the GET /notes/search handler: 400 empty_query for an empty q, otherwise the page and next_cursor.
Add loadtest/search.js, a k6 script replaying search-as-you-type queries that reports p95 latency.

verification.test_strategy: Store tests on seeded notes for term matching, ownership and ordering; handler tests for pagination and the empty query; the k6 script is run by hand before release.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR and run the 0047 down migration to drop the index.

acceptance_criteria.statement: GET /notes/search?q=alpha beta returns only the caller's notes whose title or body contains both alpha and beta.
GET /notes/search returns at most 50 notes per page, newest first, with next_cursor set when more remain.
GET /notes/search never returns a note owned by another user.
GET /notes/search with an empty q returns HTTP 400 with error code empty_query.
GET /notes/search keeps p95 latency within the service latency budget under production load.

risks_and_assumptions: Postgres full-text search is fast enough at the current notes volume.

catching_examples.note: ac-search-p95-in-budget is not concretely verifiable: no budget value is given anywhere, so no executor can decide pass/fail.
ac-search-p95-in-budget sounds measurable but is vague: the latency budget is undefined and production load has no load profile or measurement window.
The criterion keeping p95 latency within the service latency budget is untestable: which budget, at what load, measured over what window?

ac-search-p95-in-budget names a percentile but no number: neither the issue nor the plan states the budget, the load or the window, so an executor cannot decide whether it passed. State a figure such as p95 under 150 ms at 20 requests per second against a seeded 10,000-note account, or make it non-blocking.

non_catching_examples.note: ac-search-p95-in-budget needs the k6 script wired into CI, not run by hand before release.
The GIN index migration is built without CONCURRENTLY and locks writes on a large notes table.
ac-search-p95-in-budget is unquantified and ambiguous; a mismatch between staging and production hardware makes any figure unsupported.
ac-search-page: also test that the last page carries no next_cursor.
The web client calls it on every keystroke; the plan does not debounce or cancel in-flight searches.
Document GET /notes/search, next_cursor and the empty_query error in api/openapi.yaml.
